deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 154, 1983-84): Grothendieck is studying a system Σ of n pseudo-lines D_1..D_n in a real projective plane X (topological model RP^2), i.e. an arrangement of pseudolines. He builds several combinatorial-topological surfaces ('cartes', 'déploiements'), called 𝒳_0, 𝒳_1, 𝒳'_1, 𝒳_2, 𝒳_3. These are cellular surfaces encoding the relative positions of the lines. The next page adds their principal (partly ramified) coverings with group the dihedral group 𝔻_{2n} attached to the polygons Pol(D), which are the 'ultimate unfoldings'.

This page describes 𝒳_3. It closely resembles 𝒳_2, the surface 'with cusps on the boundary', as opposed to the cusp-free ones 𝒳_0, 𝒳_1, 𝒳'_1.

Vertices and their order. 𝒳_2 has vertices for the 'superposed' relative positions (the admitted 'false', degenerate positions). In 𝒳_3 these are replaced as follows. For a fixed D_i one adds a perturbed copy D'_i. This gives 2n 'supercritical' relative positions, indexed by where the virtual intersection point D_i ∩ D'_i falls: on one of 2n facets (edges of a 2n-gon). As before, every vertex has order (valence) 4, as for a crossing in a simple arrangement.

Pseudo-lines become Möbius bands. Each pseudo-line D_i of 𝒳_2 is replaced in 𝒳_3 by a Möbius band. Starting from 𝒳'_1 one orients ('dirige') the supercritical faces and makes identifications. A 'parallel' to the boundary, together with the boundary, then cuts out this band. This is the familiar fact that a regular neighbourhood of a pseudoline in RP^2 is a Möbius band.

Relation to the plane X. There is now a map 𝒳_3 → X such that the inverse image of X_1 is the right thing, including the D_i. However, unlike 𝒳'_1, this does not give a differentiable representation of Σ = (X, Σ). It gives rather a representation of a suitable tubular neighbourhood of Σ in X.

Drawback. Some singular faces do not arise from the others in the expected way. So 𝒳_3 cannot be read off from the internal combinatorics of the local system of polygons Pol(D). This local system appears to be the system, for each line D, of the cyclic/dihedral data of its 2n half-edges or directions. That is why (next page) he hopes to dispense with 𝒳_2 and 𝒳_3 in favour of 𝒳'_1 and its covering.

Purpose. He is seeking a canonical cell-surface model of a pseudoline arrangement, recoverable purely from local combinatorial data with dihedral symmetry. This is a step toward a combinatorial/'anabelian-style' description of arrangements and their moduli.
errors: No outright mathematical error is visible.
The text is a sketch; the identifications defining 𝒳_3 are only gestured at and cannot be checked.
Grothendieck himself flags a gap: he has not determined the supercritical faces of 𝒳_3 ('je n'ai pas vu les faces ... de 𝒳_3').
Grothendieck also flags that 𝒳_3 fails to be expressible via the local system of Pol(D).

ideas.what: Encoding an arrangement of n pseudolines in RP^2 by auxiliary cellular surfaces whose vertices are 4-valent and correspond to (super)critical relative positions of lines.
ideas.modern_name: Cell complexes / dual tilings of pseudoline arrangements (cf. wiring diagrams, zonotopal tilings of a 2n-gon, Bohne–Dress correspondence)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences, 1980s); Bohne/Dress (zonotopal tilings ~1989-92); Ringel, Grünbaum (earlier)

ideas.what: Replacing each pseudoline by its Möbius-band tubular neighbourhood, bounded by the boundary and a 'parallel' to it.
ideas.modern_name: Regular neighbourhood of a one-sided curve in RP^2

ideas.what: Using a perturbed copy D'_i and the position of the virtual intersection D_i∩D'_i among 2n facets to resolve a degenerate ('superposed') position into 2n supercritical positions.
ideas.modern_name: Resolution of degenerate configurations by small perturbation; links in the 2n-gon / dihedral symmetry of the space of directions

ideas.what: Local system of polygons Pol(D) with dihedral group 𝔻_{2n}, and principal 𝔻_{2n}-coverings of the surfaces as 'ultimate unfoldings'.
ideas.modern_name: Dihedral covering / combinatorial local system on an arrangement

missed.claim: Grothendieck sought a cell-surface model of a pseudoline arrangement determined by the internal combinatorics of the local system Pol(D). He found that 𝒳_3 (Möbius-band thickening) fails this, and left the faces of 𝒳_3 undetermined.
missed.quote: de sorte que 𝒳_3 ne se prête pas à une interprétation en termes de la combinatoire interne du système local des Pol(D)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a criterion — reconstructibility from local dihedral data — for comparing his models with zonotopal tilings and Salvetti-type complexes. It is minor, but would interest historians of oriented-matroid theory.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working sketch of one of several auxiliary surfaces for pseudoline arrangements. The constructions (4-valent vertices, Möbius-band neighbourhoods) are natural. The page's value lies in documenting Grothendieck's little-known 1983-84 program on pseudolines, not in a new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: the cusp-free surfaces are probably '𝒳_0, 𝒳_1, 𝒳'_1', not '𝒳_3, 𝒳_1, 𝒳'_1'; the next page lists exactly 𝒳_0, 𝒳_1, 𝒳'_1, 𝒳_2, 𝒳_3.
'faces superpositiques' is likely 'faces supercritiques' (cf. 'positions relatives supercritiques').
'voisinage tubulaire conv.' is probably 'voisinage tubulaire convenable'.
'faces singulières naissant pas des' probably reads '... ne naissent pas des ... les autres'.
'La [ps] droite' should read 'La pseudo-droite D_i de 𝒳_2'.
